query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Elevated temperature promotes preferential oxidation at the interphase boundaries of the eutectic high‐entropy alloy, forming brittle oxide films that crack under mechanical wear. This results in the breakdown of the protective passive layer and exposes fresh material to corrosive attack, causing synergistically accelerated degradation.
generation.material_initial_state: A multi‐phase eutectic high‐entropy alloy with intact, uniform passive films and ductile matrix phases separated by well-defined phase boundaries.
generation.intervention: Expose the alloy to simultaneous mechanical wear and a corrosive environment at an elevated temperature that is high enough to induce interphase oxide formation, compared to a baseline condition at a lower temperature (or isolated wear/corrosion) where oxide formation is minimal.
generation.conditions: Wear (e.g., sliding or abrasive contact) combined with a corrosive medium (e.g., chloride-rich solution) under elevated temperatures that are below melting but sufficient to activate interphase oxidation; testing should also include control samples at lower or moderate temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Interphase boundaries where the formation of brittle oxide films occurs.
generation.mechanism: At elevated temperatures, oxidation is accelerated at the phase boundaries, generating brittle, crack-prone oxide layers. Under mechanical stresses from wear, these oxides crack and spall, removing passivation and exposing fresh, unoxidized alloy surfaces to the corrosive environment. This continuous cycle of oxide cracking and film renewal enhances both abrasive wear and localized corrosion, leading to a coupled, accelerated degradation process.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to baseline conditions, the total degradation will be significantly higher under the combined wear and corrosion at elevated temperature. Specifically, wear rates will increase due to the removal of the brittle oxide films and underlying material, while corrosion rates will rise as the continuously refreshing alloy surface prevents the establishment of an effective passive layer.
generation.baseline: A matched alloy sample tested under either isolated wear or corrosion at lower temperatures that do not significantly promote interphase oxide formation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies when the temperature is sufficiently high to foster interphase oxidation but remains below temperatures that would cause melting or major phase transformations. Additionally, both mechanical wear and a corrosive medium must act concurrently to enable the synergistic degradation mechanism.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative contribution of interphase oxide formation to the overall degradation process is uncertain, as are the exact thresholds of temperature and mechanical stress required for this mechanism to dominate over other potential degradation pathways.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a set of controlled tests on the eutectic high-entropy alloy by varying one factor at a time: (1) expose samples to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, (2) expose samples to the same mechanical wear and corrosion at a lower temperature, and (3) expose samples separately to only wear or only corrosion at elevated temperature. Use high-resolution microscopy (SEM/TEM) and compositional analysis (XPS) to examine the presence, thickness, and location of oxide films, particularly at phase boundaries.
measurements: Corrosion rate (e.g., via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy or potentiodynamic polarization)
Oxide film composition and thickness (using XPS and TEM)
Crack density and distribution at interphase boundaries (via SEM imaging)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples tested under elevated temperature with simultaneous wear and corrosion do not exhibit preferential brittle oxide formation at the interphase boundaries, or if their wear and corrosion rates do not significantly exceed those of the baseline conditions (i.e., if degradation rates are not synergistically higher), then the hypothesized mechanism is falsified.
